messages:
alice: Heads-up — after the routing weight tweak at 09:12 the console heatmap LCP jumped on EU canary. Multiple users reporting ~2.5s -> 6s.
ben: Seen it too, thanks. Charts are stuttering and some tiles never finish. Any recent bundle changes?
carla: No bundle deploys from frontend in the last 24h. We did change routing policy to prefer west-eu for some read routes.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: routing-weight-v2 applied to 30% of traffic at 09:10.
dmitri: Telemetry shows a big spike in /api/metrics/tile requests from the console around 09:11. 503s from telemetry-gateway and retries flooding the frontend. Log excerpt: `telemetry-gateway: upstream_error: 503 (rate_limit)`
eva: If telemetry errors are slow, the client falls back to a heavier path that triggers full chart rehydrate — that would explain both LCP and CPU jank.
alice: Repro steps: open dashboard -> heatmap -> spinner for ~4s then partial render, CPU climbs to 80%. Happens only on canary routing.
ben: Can confirm with instrumented session. Stacktrace points to chart init waiting on `fetch('/api/metrics/tile?range=...')` which retries 3x before giving up. We probably shouldn't block critical paint on telemetry fetch.
carla: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: change routing policy back or increase telemetry-gateway quota for canary. Which is quicker?
dmitri: Increasing quota needs ops approval, could take 20–30m. Reverting routing-weight is 2 clicks — I can do that now if we want immediate relief.
alice: Do it. Revert to old routing policy and pause the canary. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary rollback: routing-weight-v2 rolled back to 0% at 09:18.
sam: Reverted — monitoring now. Telemetry 503s dropping, frontend retries lower. Heatmap LCP back to ~2.8s for sampled sessions.
eva: Followups we should consider: make chart hydration non-blocking (render placeholder and stream tiles), add a short-circuit if telemetry returns 5xx (use cached tiles), and add a client-side exponential backoff with jitter to avoid retry storms.
ben: Also audit paths that fetch telemetry during initial render — move non-essential calls to afterFirstPaint.
carla: I'll open a RFC with proposed changes: code split for chart-init, fallback cache usage, and retry policy. Also propose a temporary canary policy change: route telemetry reads to an alternate gateway (telemetry-staging) for small % so we can validate routing-induced issues.
dmitri: For immediate ops: can we add a per-canary quota override while we test? If so, we can re-run the canary safely.
alice: Good idea. Create a small runbook: steps to revert, how to snapshot telemetry gateway, thresholds to auto-rollback. Keep it <= 6 steps.
sam: I'll draft the runbook and the quick patch (client short-circuit) as a follow-up PR — will link after tests.
eva: One more note: the console telemetry tracer added in last week might be amplifying calls (double-reporting on error). Let's verify instrumentation side-effects before re-enabling canary at scale.
carla: Thanks everyone. Action items: sam PR for short-circuit (P0), carla RFC (P1), dmitri ask ops about quota override (P1), ben to add afterFirstPaint tickets (P2).
alice: Closing loop — keep posting perf numbers to #perf-alerts. If numbers reappear after revert, escalate to oncall.
